title: Centralised logs: Elastic Stack, Loki and Graylog

videos.script: Lesson 8 made every log line a record. This lesson decides where those records go, and the three answers people give most. {{three}} Loki, which indexes almost nothing and reads lines when asked. Elasticsearch, which indexes every field of every line as it arrives. And Graylog, a log product built on that same kind of index. {{stores}} The lab sends the same lines to all three at once, through one change to the Collector. You ask each one the same questions. Which charges failed. How many lines each service wrote. And everything one failed checkout left behind, found by its trace id in all three. {{questions}} Then you look at what each one costs to run, because that, more than any feature, is how teams choose. {{cost}}
